title: Directive on Public Corporate Governance of ICT
summary: Connect security to the department's ICT governance system, investment choices and realised public value.
outcomes: Use the 2022 CGICT framework's structures and principles.
Evaluate security within a complete ICT business case.
Monitor benefits, performance and corrective decisions.

realExample.title: Court Online rollout and performance reporting
realExample.documentedOutcome: The government's 2024/25 performance data records Court Online rollout and explains accelerated delivery after the system stabilised.
realExample.discussion: Use the recorded rollout to distinguish installation outputs from the benefits of a usable justice service. Define the evidence needed for access, reliability, staff readiness and realised service improvement.
realExample.scope: An official reported delivery outcome; classroom benefit and security questions are analytical, not claims about unpublished court controls.

units.title: Integrate ICT into departmental governance
objectives: Explain the role of EXCO and the ICT steering committee.
Connect ICT objectives to the departmental mandate.
Distinguish principles, practices and the governance system.

chapters.title: ICT is governed as part of the department
chapters.bodyHtml:
The 2022 framework places ICT governance within the department's corporate governance. Its purpose is to help ICT support the strategic mandate, service delivery and value from resources. It distinguishes governance from day-to-day ICT management.

EXCO provides the highest departmental oversight described in the framework; the ICT steering committee develops and monitors the departmental arrangements and reports pertinent matters. The Head of Department is the governance champion, while the Head of ICT manages the ICT function and provides relevant executive reporting.

Use these relationships to route a security issue. A patch backlog may be managed operationally; an unsupported system that threatens a statutory service and needs replacement funding requires a governance decision. The DISO should connect the technical condition to the mandate and the authority that can act.

chapters.title: Principles become practices through a system
chapters.bodyHtml:
The framework distinguishes principles, practices and a governance system. Principles guide decisions; practices describe actions and responsibilities; the system provides the structures and mechanisms through which leadership evaluates, directs and monitors ICT.

Apply this to a digital permit service. The strategic objective may be timely, accessible decisions. Practices include an approved plan, accountable investment, risk assessment and performance review. The system connects service owners, ICT, finance, governance forums and assurance so those practices actually operate.

A diagram of committees is not sufficient. Check whether a service problem can move through a decision, receive resources and return as an implemented improvement. Where the path fails, repair the decision interface rather than adding another forum with the same unclear mandate.

chapters.title: Alignment is a traceable relationship
chapters.bodyHtml:
An ICT plan should explain which departmental outcome each investment supports and how success will be assessed. 'Modernisation' is too broad unless it connects to a specific improvement such as reduced decision delay, more reliable records or a usable service channel.

Include security in the same relationship. A control can enable a service by protecting trustworthy decisions and continuity; it also consumes resources and may affect usability. State those trade-offs in the business case.

Review alignment when priorities change. If a service is retired, a previously justified investment may need adjustment. If a new statutory function depends on an old platform, the platform's risk and capacity become part of the new mandate. Preserve the decision and its assumptions so later changes can be understood.

application.title: Trace a digital justice investment to public value
application.instructionsHtml:
Fictional case: a department proposes a R20 million electronic case system. Its business case lists servers and licences but gives no baseline for filing delays, unavailable records or staff readiness.

Spend about 60 minutes creating an outcome-to-investment map and a governance route for three security and service decisions.
application.deliverable: One alignment map and three decision briefs.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Define the service outcome and baseline, such as filing access and reliable retrieval, then identify capabilities and measures. Do not use equipment purchase alone as the benefit.

Route operational configuration to ICT management and material funding/risk choices through the actual steering and EXCO arrangements.

Assign benefit owners and dependencies, including staff adoption and records quality. Preserve assumptions for later review.

reflection.prompt: Which current ICT project cannot clearly name the service outcome it is meant to improve?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Write one outcome, a baseline and the accountable benefit owner.

quiz.title: Integrate ICT into departmental governance — knowledge check

questions.name: M06-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Where does the 2022 framework place corporate governance of ICT?

answers.textHtml: Within the department's corporate governance arrangements
answers.feedbackHtml: ICT supports the departmental mandate and needs leadership oversight.

answers.textHtml: As an exclusively technical matter delegated outside corporate leadership
answers.feedbackHtml: The framework connects ICT with the department's corporate governance.

answers.textHtml: As the supplier's responsibility whenever infrastructure is outsourced
answers.feedbackHtml: Outsourcing does not remove departmental governance.

answers.textHtml: As an asset-register exercise completed once equipment is recorded
answers.feedbackHtml: An inventory supports governance but is not the whole governance system.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: ICT supports the departmental mandate and needs leadership oversight.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: Which issue most clearly requires a governance investment decision?

answers.textHtml: An unsupported platform threatens a critical service and needs funded replacement
answers.feedbackHtml: Escalate material service and resource decisions through the proper authority.

answers.textHtml: A routine approved password reset
answers.feedbackHtml: That is operational.

answers.textHtml: A standard log export
answers.feedbackHtml: That is a routine task.

answers.textHtml: A helpdesk ticket spelling correction
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not set investment direction.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Escalate material service and resource decisions through the proper authority.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: Which is a benefit rather than a procurement output?

answers.textHtml: A measured reduction in time to retrieve complete case records
answers.feedbackHtml: Benefits describe useful changes in the service.

answers.textHtml: Twenty new servers delivered
answers.feedbackHtml: Delivery is an output; the benefit is the resulting service improvement.

answers.textHtml: A licence invoice paid
answers.feedbackHtml: Payment records expenditure rather than the service benefit.

answers.textHtml: Staff attendance at the implementation workshop
answers.feedbackHtml: Attendance is an activity measure, not the demonstrated case-retrieval improvement.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Benefits describe useful changes in the service.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: What should an ICT plan connect each investment to?

answers.textHtml: A departmental outcome and a way to assess it
answers.feedbackHtml: Alignment must be traceable.

answers.textHtml: Only the supplier catalogue
answers.feedbackHtml: Products are means.

answers.textHtml: Only the budget line number
answers.feedbackHtml: A cost code does not explain value.

answers.textHtml: A vague promise of modernisation
answers.feedbackHtml: The outcome needs definition.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Alignment must be traceable.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What is missing from a committee diagram with no functioning decision path?

answers.textHtml: An operating governance system
answers.feedbackHtml: The structures must evaluate, direct and monitor actual work.

answers.textHtml: More frequent meetings with the same undefined decision rights
answers.feedbackHtml: Frequency does not create authority or a usable escalation path.

answers.textHtml: A larger technical inventory without assigned decision responsibilities
answers.feedbackHtml: More information alone does not make governance operate.

answers.textHtml: A new reporting template with no owner for the requested actions
answers.feedbackHtml: Presentation cannot replace the decision and accountability system.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The structures must evaluate, direct and monitor actual work.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: A project's service is retired. What should happen to its investment assumptions?

answers.textHtml: Review them against the changed mandate
answers.feedbackHtml: Maintain alignment as service needs change.

answers.textHtml: Keep them forever because they were once approved
answers.feedbackHtml: The basis has changed.

answers.textHtml: Delete all decision history
answers.feedbackHtml: History explains the original choice.

answers.textHtml: Assume the vendor decides the new purpose
answers.feedbackHtml: The department must decide.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Maintain alignment as service needs change.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which elements strengthen an outcome-to-investment map? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: A baseline and target service result
answers.feedbackHtml: They make the benefit assessable.

answers.textHtml: A named benefit owner and dependencies
answers.feedbackHtml: They make delivery accountable.

answers.textHtml: Only licence quantities
answers.feedbackHtml: Those are outputs.

answers.textHtml: An assumption that installation guarantees adoption
answers.feedbackHtml: Staff and process readiness matter.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A useful map goes beyond procurement.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which statements correctly connect security to ICT governance? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Security can protect the reliability of a public decision
answers.feedbackHtml: It supports service value.

answers.textHtml: Control cost and usability effects belong in the business case
answers.feedbackHtml: Trade-offs should be visible.

answers.textHtml: Security has no relationship to the service mandate
answers.feedbackHtml: Its consequences affect that mandate.

answers.textHtml: Every security choice must bypass the normal governance system
answers.feedbackHtml: That fragments decisions.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Assess security as part of the complete service.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: The framework distinguishes principles, practices and the system that enables their operation.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: These are related but different parts of governance.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. These are related but different parts of governance.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: These are related but different parts of governance.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Purchasing the planned equipment proves the intended public benefit has been realised.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Delivered outputs need to be connected to measured service outcomes.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Delivered outputs need to be connected to measured service outcomes.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Delivered outputs need to be connected to measured service outcomes.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the framework concept to its function.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The components work together to connect mandate and results.

questions.name: M06-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: An investment should trace to a departmental [[1]] and an accountable benefit [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Traceability and ownership make alignment usable.

units.title: Evaluate investments and monitor realised benefits
objectives: Set benefit, risk and service review conditions.
Use evidence to redirect or stop ineffective work.

chapters.title: Evaluate the whole cost and dependency
chapters.bodyHtml:
Compare options against the same service requirement. Include implementation, data preparation, training, operation, support, security, recovery and exit. A low licence price may conceal costly migration or dependence on a supplier who alone can retrieve the data.

State assumptions and sensitivity. If the expected benefit depends on eighty percent staff adoption, identify how adoption will be supported and measured. If a cheaper design has longer recovery time, show whether that meets the service's agreed needs.

Consider a phased option when it produces a complete usable service increment and resolves material uncertainty. Avoid a pilot that cannot be maintained, exported or assessed. The decision should explain why the chosen option gives acceptable value and risk within the department's constraints.

chapters.title: Set conditions before approval
chapters.bodyHtml:
The framework's value-and-benefit principle calls for expected value to be identified and realised. Before approving an investment, agree the benefit owner, baseline, measures, dependencies and review dates. Include control and service acceptance conditions.

Acceptance should follow the real operating journey. Can authorised staff complete the service, correct a record, recover after interruption and obtain the required reports? Can the department maintain and exit the solution? These questions reveal whether a delivery is ready to support its intended benefit.

Preserve the approved scope and material changes. If a supplier removes a recovery feature or changes information use, compare the new proposal with the original decision. A changed contract can require a changed risk and value assessment.

chapters.title: Monitor and act on the result
chapters.bodyHtml:
Report actuals against the baseline and target, with the period, population and data source. Explain gaps and the confidence of the measure. A reduced queue may reflect a useful improvement, fewer applications or incomplete reporting; the interpretation needs context.

Governance should act when benefits do not emerge. Options include correcting adoption problems, changing scope, improving controls, renegotiating delivery or stopping an ineffective investment through the proper process. Protect records and service continuity during any transition.

The Court Online example is useful because official performance reporting explains delivery progress and its context. Apply the same discipline to your own project: record what was delivered, what changed for users and what remains to be demonstrated. Keep plans and achieved results distinct.

application.title: Review a platform six months after launch
application.instructionsHtml:
A fictional permit platform costR8 million to install. The target was to reduce average decision time from 30 to 15 days. The dashboard reports 12 days, but excludes incomplete cases and the busiest district. Only half of staff use it; the supplier charges separately for export.

Spend about 60 minutes preparing a benefit-review paper with corrected questions and a recommended decision.
application.deliverable: A two-page investment review with a corrective action plan.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Do not accept the 12-day figure as a like-for-like result. Restore the agreed population, period and definition, and explain exclusions.

Assess adoption barriers, full operating/exit costs and the effect on residents. Assign data correction, staff support and export/exit actions.

Recommend a decision based on the corrected evidence and service need. Preserve the original target and explain any approved revision rather than rewriting it to fit the result.

reflection.prompt: Which benefit measure would change most if its excluded cases were restored?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Explain the population and definition needed for a fair comparison.

quiz.title: Evaluate investments and monitor realised benefits — knowledge check

questions.name: M06-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Which cost view supports a sound investment decision?

answers.textHtml: Implementation, operation, support, recovery and exit across the service lifecycle
answers.feedbackHtml: Compare complete options against the same requirement.

answers.textHtml: Only the initial licence price
answers.feedbackHtml: The service also needs implementation, operation and eventual transition.

answers.textHtml: Only capital expenditure, assuming staff support has no cost
answers.feedbackHtml: Staff and operating capacity are material to a feasible service.

answers.textHtml: The supplier's bundled price without examining departmental integration and exit work
answers.feedbackHtml: A supplier price may omit important departmental lifecycle costs.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Compare complete options against the same requirement.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A benefit assumes eighty percent staff adoption. What belongs in the plan?

answers.textHtml: An adoption owner, support actions and a measure
answers.feedbackHtml: Make benefit dependencies explicit.

answers.textHtml: An assumption that purchase ensures use
answers.feedbackHtml: Adoption requires work.

answers.textHtml: Removal of the assumption from the record
answers.feedbackHtml: That hides a dependency.

answers.textHtml: A claim that reluctant staff are the only possible cause
answers.feedbackHtml: Usability and process conditions may matter.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Make benefit dependencies explicit.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: A dashboard excludes the busiest district. What must be checked?

answers.textHtml: Whether it remains comparable to the agreed baseline and target
answers.feedbackHtml: Population and definitions must support the comparison.

answers.textHtml: Whether the same graph format is still used
answers.feedbackHtml: Consistent presentation does not establish a comparable population.

answers.textHtml: Whether the remaining districts alone meet the target, without disclosing the exclusion
answers.feedbackHtml: The omitted district may materially change the result.

answers.textHtml: Whether last month's baseline can be silently changed to the smaller scope
answers.feedbackHtml: Definition changes need transparent treatment rather than retroactive concealment.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Population and definitions must support the comparison.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A supplier removes recovery functionality after approval. What is needed?

answers.textHtml: A review of the changed scope, risk and value
answers.feedbackHtml: Material changes can alter the original decision.

answers.textHtml: Automatic acceptance because the original approval covered the supplier
answers.feedbackHtml: Approval concerned a defined scope and assumptions, which have changed.

answers.textHtml: Only a contract-file update with no service-owner assessment
answers.feedbackHtml: Documentation alone does not evaluate the new risk and value.

answers.textHtml: A check of unchanged licence quantities while excluding recovery from acceptance
answers.feedbackHtml: Licence counts do not address the removed service capability.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Material changes can alter the original decision.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What is a useful acceptance journey?

answers.textHtml: Staff complete, correct, report and recover the actual service
answers.feedbackHtml: Acceptance should cover the service's real operating needs.

answers.textHtml: A single attractive login screenshot
answers.feedbackHtml: It does not exercise the service.

answers.textHtml: A list of promised features
answers.feedbackHtml: Promises are not operating outcomes.

answers.textHtml: A supplier demonstration using unrelated data only
answers.feedbackHtml: It may not establish the required workflow.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Acceptance should cover the service's real operating needs.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: When benefits fail to emerge, what should governance do?

answers.textHtml: Assess causes and decide correction, redirection or stopping through the proper process
answers.feedbackHtml: Monitoring must inform a decision.

answers.textHtml: Continue indefinitely to avoid admitting difficulty
answers.feedbackHtml: That can compound cost.

answers.textHtml: Delete all records of the target
answers.feedbackHtml: That destroys accountability.

answers.textHtml: Assume every shortfall is a cyberattack
answers.feedbackHtml: The evidence may indicate other causes.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Monitoring must inform a decision.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which fields make benefit reporting interpretable? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Period, population and data source
answers.feedbackHtml: They define what was measured.

answers.textHtml: Baseline, target and actual result
answers.feedbackHtml: They support a comparison.

answers.textHtml: An unexplained percentage
answers.feedbackHtml: Its meaning is unclear.

answers.textHtml: Only selected success stories
answers.feedbackHtml: They may omit the wider service result.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Report the measure's context.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which conditions strengthen an investment's exit plan? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Usable information export and ownership responsibilities
answers.feedbackHtml: They support continuity and control.

answers.textHtml: A transition plan for staff and services
answers.feedbackHtml: Exit can affect the public.

answers.textHtml: Dependence on one person's undocumented access
answers.feedbackHtml: That creates fragility.

answers.textHtml: No retained decision or data history
answers.feedbackHtml: That impedes an orderly transition.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Exit is part of lifecycle governance.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A changed service population can make a lower average misleading.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Compare like with like and explain exclusions.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Compare like with like and explain exclusions.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Compare like with like and explain exclusions.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Expected benefits and achieved benefits are the same evidence category.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. A plan states intent; an achieved result requires observation.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: A plan states intent; an achieved result requires observation.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A plan states intent; an achieved result requires observation.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the item to its investment role.

pairs.answer: Assessment of delivered value and needed action

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: These elements make investment decisions assessable.

questions.name: M06-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Compare actual benefits against the retained [[1]] using a consistent [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A comparable measure supports a defensible decision.
